RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Jordan Mercado
Member ID: W484245232
Reference Number: POC-FD00FECEC4-98407
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-11
Service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for total hip replacement (CPT 27130), as set forth in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11. The stated reason for denial was that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I respectfully disagree and submit this appeal with supporting clinical documentation showing that the applicable medical policy criteria have in fact been met.

**Governing Medical Policy**

I understand the medical necessity criteria applied to this determination are found in Excellus BlueCross BlueShield Medical Policy 7.01.96, "Hip Arthroplasty" (Current Effective Date 04/20/23). That policy states, in relevant part, that total hip replacement is considered medically necessary when:

"Tonnis Grade 3 osteoarthritis or avascular necrosis with collapse of the femoral head, or inflammatory arthropathy affecting both the femoral head and acetabulum with joint space narrowing, is present, and ALL of the following criteria have been met: 1. function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three months' duration; 2. loss of hip function secondary to osteoarthritis that interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment; and 3. failure of provider-directed, non-surgical management for at least three months (at least six months for patients with BMI greater than 40) or documentation in the medical record of the reasons that provider-directed, non-surgical management is not appropriate (e.g., collapse of the femoral head, inflammatory arthritis, advanced dysplasia). The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate."

The policy further defines non-surgical management as follows:

"Non-surgical management with regard to the treatment of hip osteoarthritis is defined as any provider-directed, non-surgical treatment that has been demonstrated in the scientific literature to be efficacious and/or is considered reasonable care in the treatment of hip pain from osteoarthritis. The types of treatment can include but are not limited to: relative rest/activity modification, weight loss, supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises, oral prescription and non-prescription medications, assistive devices (e.g., cane, crutches, walker, wheelchair), and/or intra-articular (i.e., steroid) injections."

The policy also lists specific exclusionary conditions under which total hip replacement is considered not medically necessary, including active infection, unmanageable osseous abnormality, uncontrolled comorbid medical conditions, vascular insufficiency or neuromuscular disease compromising implant stability, severe immunocompromise, Charcot joint, or the patient being on dialysis and a renal transplant list.

**Application of the Criteria to Jordan Mercado's Records**

1. *Duration and severity of symptoms (Criterion III.B.1):* Mr./Ms. Mercado has experienced 14 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest, which substantially exceeds the three-month minimum specified in the policy. Current function is limited to walking one block using a cane, which falls within the policy's own example of function-limiting pain "at short distances (e.g., ... limiting activity to two city blocks)."

2. *Loss of function / impact on activities of daily living (Criterion III.B.2):* The patient cannot put on shoes unassisted and requires a cane to ambulate. This documents loss of hip function that interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living, as required by the policy.

3. *Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management (Criterion III.B.3):* The record documents multiple modalities specifically named in the policy's own definition of non-surgical management:
   - Supervised physical therapy targeting hip abductor strengthening and gait, 12 weeks, 20 visits completed (2026-04-04 through 2026-06-27), per the physical therapy discharge note;
   - Oral NSAID therapy for 6 months with inadequate relief;
   - An intra-articular corticosteroid injection administered 2026-04-03, which provided only two weeks of partial relief;
   - Use of an assistive device (cane) for ambulation.

   These modalities meet or exceed the three-month minimum trial the policy requires (the patient's BMI of 29 does not trigger the six-month threshold reserved for patients with BMI greater than 40), and all have failed to provide durable relief.

4. *Radiographic findings consistent with the policy's severity threshold:* The weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph dated 2026-07-14 shows joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophyte formation. [The imaging report as summarized does not state an explicit Tönnis grade; Dr. Lindqvist is asked to append a statement confirming the Tönnis grade or otherwise correlating these radiographic findings to the policy's Tönnis Grade 3 description, as the policy criterion is expressed in those terms.]

5. *Absence of listed exclusionary conditions:* The record confirms no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29 (not in the range associated with any modified requirement other than the standard three-month conservative-care threshold), and non-smoker status. There is no indication in the record of osseous abnormality precluding surgery, uncontrolled comorbid medical disease, vascular insufficiency, neuromuscular disease, severe immunocompromise, Charcot joint, or dialysis/renal transplant status — the conditions the policy identifies as bases for a not-medically-necessary determination.

**Conclusion**

The attached records — the physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection records, the 2026-07-14 radiograph report, and the surgeon's clinical notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations — demonstrate that Mr./Ms. Mercado has completed a conservative treatment trial that meets the duration and content described in Excellus Medical Policy 7.01.96, and that the functional and radiographic severity criteria in that same policy are met. We ask that the denial be reversed and that prior authorization for CPT 27130 (total hip replacement) be approved.

Enclosed please find:
- Physical therapy discharge summary (2026-04-04 to 2026-06-27)
- Medication administration/prescription records documenting NSAID trial
- Corticosteroid injection record dated 2026-04-03
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph report dated 2026-07-14
- Surgeon's clinical/exam notes, Dr. Lindqvist
- [Any additional records the patient or surgeon wishes to append, e.g., a supplemental letter from Dr. Lindqvist explicitly stating the Tönnis grade]

Please notify me and Dr. Lindqvist's office in writing of the outcome of this appeal. If any additional information is needed, please contact [phone number] or [email address]. If this appeal is denied, I request a copy of the specific clinical rationale and any criteria applied beyond Medical Policy 7.01.96, and information on my right to an external appeal through New York State.

Sincerely,

Jordan Mercado
[Phone number]
